Canto 7] Accompanied by the Rasikapriya and Rasamanjari commentaries 103

May this song of Hari <note>original: "Hari"</note> as spoken by Jayadeva,
Cause the impurities of the Kali Age to be pacified.

This moon, mimicking the radiance of Murari’s <note>original: "Murari"</note> lotus-face—which had become pale from separation—
Though it conceals the pain, acts as a friend to the Mind-Born <note>original: "Manobhuva"</note> <gloss>Kamadeva, the God of Love</gloss>,
And greatly intensifies the agony of passion within my heart.

The battle of love; there, the resolute one is steady. Sri. May this composition of Jayadeva, depicting the inverted union <note>original: "viparita-rati"</note>, pacify the impurities of the Kali Age, bringing about tranquility. And so it is said in the Sangitaraja: "Where the Sri raga <note>original: "Sri-raga"</note> is the musical mode and the rhythm is the drutamanthaka <note>original: "drutamanthaka"</note>; where there is a description of Vasudeva <note>original: "Vasudeva"</note> and the actions of love; where there are poetic syllables and rhythmic structures, that is known as a superior composition. Hari’s limitless radiance is like the champaka <note>original: "campaka"</note> flower, called the crest-jewel." Thus is the fourteenth composition named Hari-amita-champaka-shekhara. Now, Radha, tormented by separation, addresses the moon: "In separation." 'Aye' is a soft address. O friend, this moon expands the agony of passion in my heart. How is it? It is a friend to the Mind-Born, Kamadeva. She speaks through the memory of her separation from Murari. How is it? It has a radiance like that of Murari’s lotus-face, which grew pale from separation. For this very reason, even though it conceals the pain, it does so. This is what is meant: by possessing the facial radiance of my beloved who is pale from separation, even if it destroys my pain, as a friend of love, it causes pain indeed. Although it is not to be accepted, since it remains in that state, and knowing he is now attached to another, I cannot endure it.

Hamsalilaka <note>original: "Hamsalilaka"</note>. "A drop, a particle, an ocean" says the Amarakosha. Sri Jayadeva. The play of Hari, Krishna, spoken by Jayadeva, may it destroy the impurities of the Kali Age, meaning for the listeners and readers, may it bring them to an end. Now she says that the moon also causes more suffering: "In separation." 'Aye' is used in sorrow. This visible moon expands, to a great extent, the agony of passion, the pain of love, in my heart. What kind of moon? One whose radiance is that of the lotus-face of Krishna, which became pale due to my separation from him. And so, seeing the moon, which is like the lotus-face of such a Krishna, causes extreme pain due to the memory of Krishna’s lotus-face. What is it doing? It is concealing the pain. And so, upon seeing the moon, there is an eradication of discernment, and the mind remembers him, even though he has committed an offense against me. She gives the reason for its being a cause of suffering: "of the Mind-Born," the friend of Kamadeva. And so, because I did not follow Krishna even when he was nearby, by violating the command of Kamadeva, Kamadeva has become my enemy. The moon also causes pain, wishing to assist him, is the idea. The moon is famous as being born from the mind <note>original: "manas"</note>, just as Kamadeva <note>original: "Manasija"</note> is. Due to them being brothers, there is friendship between Kamadeva and the moon, hence the use of the term 'Manobhuva'. And so the Veda says: "The moon was born from the mind, the sun from the eye." Vedana means knowledge and pain, as well as fear, anger, sorrow, confusion, and memory.
